# Rearview camera installation and wiring

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Locate power, pop clips for attachment points, then splice in wire with spade connectors. [t915]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Locate the power supply to the rear license plate lights by tucking your head under the back bumper.
2. Identify where the passenger side light lead connects via a small plastic clip on a metal flange hanging from the body work.
3. Pop out this plastic clip without breaking it to create two attachment points: one for mounting the relay and another for splicing into the power supply.

_Procedure reported by [t915]._

## Tools

- Side cutters [t915]
- Female spade connectors (automotive wire) [t915]
- Male spade connectors (for relay) [t915]

## Parts

- SPDT Relay [t915]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Drop the spare tire to the ground if it obstructs access under the bumper. [t915]
- Use a self-tapping machine screw and ring connector to ground the relay to the metal flange. [t915]
